analysis.title: Market Update US, Europe & Asia
key_insights: US equities fell on Monday 11/16 and ended near worst levels: S&P 500 -1.92% to 7416.59, Nasdaq -2.49%, Dow -1.41%. Equal-weight RSP beat the cap-weighted index by 90 bp, extending last week's relative outperformance.
The AI trade was broadly weaker, with semis, memory and neoclouds selling off sharply. Three of the Mag 7 were down 3% or more. SOX is down about 9% over the past three sessions.

The NVDA leadership transition is a high-profile overhang. The company is expected to deliver another beat and raise on Tuesday, but results are unlikely to ease concerns about AI infrastructure funding and tighter export controls. A White House proposal to close a key export loophole was in focus.
Supply is on the front burner: the Anthropic IPO is due later this week and is reportedly 6x oversubscribed.

The lower rate backdrop is not supporting the broadening-out trade, parts of which are under valuation scrutiny. Last week yields backed up on a hotter CPI and hawkish Fedspeak, which, with dollar strength, raised concerns about tighter financial conditions.

Treasuries were mostly firmer with the curve steepening, and short-end yields fell 4-5 bp. The dollar index rose 0.2%, back near pre-Liberation Day levels. Gold fell 0.9%, silver 4.6%, bitcoin futures 5.7% and WTI crude 3.2%.

Macro: November Empire State manufacturing missed as new orders slowed sharply, though employment expanded and prices paid and received fell m/m but remain elevated. Cleveland Fed's Hammack said inflation is moving in the wrong direction and she prefers smaller policy adjustments. Warsh's remarks did not address monetary policy.

The week's calendar: Tuesday retail sales, import prices, industrial production and homebuilder sentiment. Wednesday housing starts, building permits, pending home sales and the October FOMC minutes. Thursday Philly Fed and jobless claims. Friday University of Michigan sentiment and inflation expectations. A Trump/Xi/Putin meeting is set for Thursday.

Europe closed lower and near the worst levels of the day. Germany -0.57%, France -0.20%, UK -0.19%. Oil fell despite new tanker incidents in the Strait of Hormuz, as traders focused on an IEA warning that global demand could shrink in 2026.

Asia was mostly lower, with sharp declines in Korean and Taiwanese tech. Nikkei -2.42%, Samsung -4.5%, SK Hynix almost -8.0%, TSMC -5.7%. Reports that Nvidia's ousted CEO Huang was eyeing a return lifted early trading before doubts about the sector's debt returned.

China's October activity data disappointed: industrial output and retail sales growth slowed from September and investment contracted by more than expected. Japan's Q3 GDP contracted 0.1%. Thailand's Q3 GDP grew 2.9% y/y, below expectations.

Corporate events: Telus +12.2% on an unsolicited Quebecor proposal. Tyson +8.7% on an FQ4 beat. Summit Therapeutics -16.5% on an FDA complete response letter for ivonescimab. Robinhood -7.5% on a report that Kalshi bought FB Securities and plans equity trading. Diamondback -4.1% on a ~$5B Double Eagle acquisition. New World Development -40.8% on a HK$24.9B rights issue.

market_movers.rationale: RBC Capital Markets upgraded from sector perform, citing management's Medicare starts recovery strategy and renewed focus on margins. Stock +2.5%.
William Blair downgraded USA Rare Earth from outperform, citing feedstock shortages and sales and margin estimates pushed out into 2028. Stock -12.6%.
Deutsche Bank upgraded Croda to buy from hold.
Jefferies upgraded Holcim to buy from hold.
Goldman Sachs downgraded Svenska Cellulosa to sell from neutral. Stock -3.5%.
Jefferies downgraded Ibstock to underperform from hold. Stock -5.3%.
Barclays downgraded Clariant to equal weight from overweight.
Barclays upgraded Wacker Chemie to overweight from equal weight.

earnings_insights: Tyson Foods (TSN) FQ4 earnings and revenue beat. Volumes were better though ASPs decreased, and International was a bright spot. The FY27 operating income guide brackets consensus, with a better Beef segment guide. Stock +8.7%.
GXO Logistics (GXO) issued 2030 targets ahead of its investor day: 7%+ organic revenue CAGR and 6.5%+ adjusted EBITA margin. Stock +4.6%.
Summit Therapeutics (SMMT) received an FDA complete response letter for ivonescimab plus chemotherapy in 2L EGFR-mutant NSCLC. Stock -16.5%.
NVDA is expected to report on Tuesday 11/17 after the close and is expected to deliver another beat and raise (expectation, not a print).
Uniper expects its existing portfolio to support 2027 adj. EBITDA of EUR1.2-1.5B vs FactSet EUR1.41B.

macro_indicators.reading: Missed expectations; new orders slowed sharply, employment index expanded
macro_indicators.interpretation: Weak new orders point to softer manufacturing demand, while elevated prices paid and received keep inflation pressure in view.

macro_indicators.reading: Industrial output and retail sales growth slowed from September; investment contracted by more than expected
macro_indicators.interpretation: Weak domestic demand, with house prices also falling from September.
The economy contracted as consumption stayed weak on inflation and poor weather.
US 2s10s is 31 bp, and the report says the curve steepened on Monday.

crypto_views: Bitcoin futures fell 5.7% on Monday but came off the worst levels. Cryptocurrencies were back under pressure in Asia after the weekend's slide.
